author: kovacsv
content: Putting together a working action is a bit tricky. An action is basically a set of commands that run in the cloud on the repository. The complexity here is that you need the development kits to make it compile, but the development kits can't be in the open source repo because of licensing issues. My approach to resolve this is to upload the devkits to a server (like dropbox) and add the url as a secret to the repository. This way the action can access it, but there is no publicly available links for the devkits. If your repository is public, I'm happy to help setting this up.

author: kovacsv
content:
It depends on a couple of things, for example the role of the person in the repository.

**Collaborators:**
Right now there are 4 collaborators for the repository (<@900814845191000115>, <@840956366989951037>, <@693250122431201320> and myself). These people can do whatever they want, even committing directly to the main branch. I would say as a rule of thumb that if you are 100% sure you are doing the right thing, just push it to main. If you need a review the best if you create a branch from main, open a Pull Request, add the relevant people as reviewer, and merge the Pull Request only after the review.

**Non-collaborators:**
Non-collaborators' only option is to crate a fork (so they have their own version of the repository under their name), create a branch in that fork and open a Pull Request with the modifications. Only collaborators can merge these kind of Pull Requests, so everything is always reviewed.

author: thekaushikls
content:
Rhino/ Grasshopper needs to be restarted multiple times while developing nodes / plugins.
Here is a script that I use (Windows only), that does it for me.

Save the contents as a `.bat` file, and run it directly from VSCode, or by double clicking it.

```Shell
REM Kills all open Rhino files. Does NOT save anything, use at your own risk
taskkill /im Rhino.exe /t /f

REM Run build script using IronPython v2.7.9+, and copies to Grasshopper>SpecialFolders
ipy "build_module.py" "C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Roaming\Grasshopper\Libraries"

REM Launch Rhino and Grasshopper
"C:\Program Files\Rhino 7\System\Rhino.exe" /nosplash /runscript="_-Grasshopper Banner Disable Window Load Window Show _Enter"
```

author: kovacsv
content:
🎉 Good news, Folks!

After a week of trial and error i managed to make the Add-On automatically code signed and notarized. No more silly warnings for users. The hardest twelve lines of code in my life, but it seems working now. 🙂 Thanks for the help <@423113258229039105>!

```
echo ${{ secrets.CODE_SIGN_CERT }} | base64 --decode > certificate.p12
security create-keychain -p KeyChainPass notarization.keychain
security default-keychain -s notarization.keychain
security unlock-keychain -p KeyChainPass notarization.keychain
security import certificate.p12 -k notarization.keychain -P ${{ secrets.CODE_SIGN_CERT_PWD }}  -T /usr/bin/codesign
security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k KeyChainPass notarization.keychain
codesign -s "Developer ID Application: enzyme apd Limited (${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }})" -f -vvv --deep --timestamp --entitlements archicad-addon/Tools/addon.entitlements --options runtime archicad-addon/Build/RelWithDebInfo/TapirAddOn_AC${{ matrix.params.acVersion }}_Mac.bundle
xcrun notarytool store-credentials "addon.notarization" --apple-id ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }} --password ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID_PWD }} --team-id ${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }}
ditto -c -k --keepParent archicad-addon/Build/RelWithDebInfo/TapirAddOn_AC${{ matrix.params.acVersion }}_Mac.bundle archicad-addon/Build/RelWithDebInfo/TapirAddOn_AC${{ matrix.params.acVersion }}_Mac.zip
xcrun notarytool submit archicad-addon/Build/RelWithDebInfo/TapirAddOn_AC${{ matrix.params.acVersion }}_Mac.zip --wait --keychain-profile "addon.notarization"
xcrun stapler staple archicad-addon/Build/RelWithDebInfo/TapirAddOn_AC${{ matrix.params.acVersion }}_Mac.bundle
rm archicad-addon/Build/RelWithDebInfo/TapirAddOn_AC${{ matrix.params.acVersion }}_Mac.zip
```

Is there a way to send request from webbrowser (from external servel) to localhost:19723 to connect to archicad json API?

author: kovacsv
content:
The short answer is no.

The longer answer: It doesn't work because of security reasons. Imagine a website that can do anything on your local computer, that would be a huge security risk. Depending on what you are planning to do you have some options though:
- You can expose your computer to the public internet, so everyone and every website can access it. You need a fix ip provider for this since the ip address is changing all the time. You probably don't want to do this.
- The best way to connect AC with an external website is to write an Add-On that uses the Browser Control in Archicad, and communicate with the website via JSON commands. This way users would be able to open the website right from AC, so it's a more user friendly way to achieve what you want.

content: Nothing specific. Only second and third hand. Been following Python since the beta in 23. and watched it go down hill from there. I use it because it is easy to learn and provides easy access to data not available otherwise, but never for anything that can't be discontinued tomorrow. I do know that Graphisoft is exploring (just exploring the concept) of a on line store to share AddOns both free and paid. Python scripts will be a part of that if it happens. Personally, I don't think there are enough applications in Python to justify it right now. But for some specific immediate need, there might be nothing else. Don't mean to downgrade its use as it can be very valuable -- just saying -- don't expect much support from Graphisoft based on past history . THAT IS WHAT WE ARE TRYING TO CHANGE.

content: Hi <@830104603554086965> thank you so much for the offering. Let me give you a bit of background. We hit a wall very quickly as the official API was very limited

author: jbeneitez
content: Then we discovered that <@1254417128979959909> had a GitHub repository with a template that allowed to port C++ API commands into JSON calls accesible via Python. content: Then generously <@844197976430608424> (C++ dev) started helping us to port a number of C++ functions that the community found useful

author: jbeneitez
content: And our idea is to start with the Python library AND grasshopper plugin (just because the large number of users that use grasshopper at the moment in the community) and once having most of the functions, bring the access to other visual programming softwares (Blender, BeeGraphy,...) and perhaps develop an online node-base portal that uses the python API

author: jbeneitez
content: In any case <@830104603554086965> , all the content from the repository is and will be opensource and free

author: dkovacs9689
content:
Just to add to the "Display Order" topic: Yeah, this is very annoying, and there should definitely be a solution! I've had it on my wishlist for a long time, but now that we have BIMdots, I am sure you can make an add-on for it in no time!

Generally the way it works, is when elements are drawn on the screen (regardless of layers) they could cover each other up depending on drawing order. Each element type has a display order level assigned to them by default (and those default levels are really stupid). There are 14 levels, level 1 is the bottom, level 14 is the top. The only commands you have available to control it is by 5 buttons (found in the context menu when elements are selected, and on a display order toolbar): bring forward, bring to front, send backward, send to back, and assign default level.

It took significant begging to Somorjai to have him add this to the Element Information palette as a GRID project a few years ago. 😄 (before, there was no way to know)

Anyhow, what we need:
- an interface to be able to assign a number directly, instead of moving things up and down (e.g., to move things from level 12 to level 8, I would need to send backwards 4 times. instead, I just want to be able to enter the number 8 in a field, and it would get applied.
- when a number is assigned, it would also be a benefit, that I can just move everything to the same level at once, even if they started from somewhere else( e.g. if I have a wall on level 12 and another one on level 10, and I "send backward" they will be on level 11 and level 9 respectively, so it would be tricky to have them move to the same level. If I can just assign them level 8 at once, that would be easier
- We should also be able to change the default level for elements
- and to apply these settings based on filters without selection (e.g. put all walls in the entire project on level 5. or move everything on the " stairs" layer to level 11 in the entire project, etc.)
- ideally in a neat little palette

author: kovacsv
content:
<@840956366989951037> I'm wondering about the role of the tapir_py package.

I understand that the core logic (`Link`, `Parameter`, etc.) must be reimplemented in Python 2 to ensure compatibility with Grasshopper that supports Python 2 only.

What I don't see at this point is the need to implement all of the specific calls in python (`GetAllElements`, `GetElementsByClassification`, etc.). I see this as a huge amount of work, and don't see the exact benefit. Of course it would make it more convenient to implement GrassHopper nodes, but the Python script in the nodes could just operate on json objects.

So my - maybe controversial - idea is to keep the tapir_py stupid simple, containing only utility functions, so we don't have to reimplement everything in python.

author: eldelion
content:
One of the questions I mentioned is definitely related to the purpose of the tapir_py package, but from a different perspective.

I have been using the official Python package for a few projects. While I've encountered a few issues (which could be due to my own inexperience or actual shortcomings of the package), the abstraction layer it provides definitely offers several advantages:

-Objects have types, and commands include type hints, so IDEs and type checkers can infer the return type. This, combined with using the typing module/type checkers in your own code, can be very helpful.
-With commands implemented as functions or methods, IDEs can provide auto-completion.
-Operating directly on JSON is at a different abstraction level than the rest of the code, so it makes sense to handle it in a separate module.
When I use any of the additional commands in code that is longer than a few lines, I definitely prefer to have a wrapper around the commands and types I use. However, I would prefer if there were a package that provides that abstraction layer.

I’m just not sure if what I’ve outlined falls within the goals of tapir_py, or if the same package can be used with both IronPython and typed Python 3.12. (Incidentally, tapir_py already has type information in its docstrings, but I’m not sure if it's in a format that can be used by type checkers.)

author: eldelion
content:
Last week I did a bit of experimentation with Pydantic and the datamodel-code-generator. I think a possible solution for a Python 3.8++ package would be the following:
•    Use the official package for the official commands
•    Generate Pydantic types from the JSON schema
•    Write simple tapir commands (The code will be pretty simple, we mostly need good function headers for IDE type hints / Autocomplete)
•    We create type converters, that create official types from tapir types and vica-versa. I made POC versions: 
https://github.com/SzamosiMate/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/python-package-pydantic/type_converters.py
However, for this approach to work, I think we need some changes to the JSON schema of the ArchiCAD add-on. 
•    Schema definitions with the same name should be the same or have different names (for example official propertyValue / tapir propertyValue)
•    We should extract/create more JSON objects from the list of output/input values.
o           For example: GetProjectInfo should return a PrijectInfo object instead of 2 booleans and 3 strings. Or maybe: Oneof UntitledProjectInfo | ProjectInfo, where ProjectInfo is Project   name and Oneof: TeamworkAdress | WindowsPath | MacPath
•    Similar commands and similar data should use a similar structure. For example, GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements from Tapir returns a pretty different structure from GetComponentsOfElements.

author: eldelion
content:
The topic of creating Properties came up, and I thought about it a bit. Or maybe a a bit more, than a bit. This has became a long post. Anyways I wanted to start a discussion on what are the biggest hurdels regarding property creation that tapir commands may solve, and what commands we need.
We mainly use enumerated properties (and expression based ofc), so it is easy to change the values, and the same thing is called the same in the project. The actual property modification is usually done by the BIM guys from a big excel where architects write their “wishes”.
While that is already pretty time consumeing, the real pain starts when we have a big project modelled across 8-12 files. While there is a property export/import functionality, it does not modify the existing properties, but overwrites it. This is mostly fine for expression based properties (well if we don’t use them for graphic overrides etc) but for properties with instance data this can mean the loss of data, so we never use it.
We open the files one by one, and create/modify the new options. We are trying to keep the options the same across all files, but it is just a daunting task, and errors always happen. And is an error happens we can not generate lists or legends from the whole complex as those lists will not work.
We would love to have tools to help this. To automate the management of properties in addition to the create property, we need ways to modify the existing definitions.
The following things have to be uniform uniform across projects in order for lists from the whole complex to work:
•    The name on the property, and the property group
•    The order of the properties (I am not sure this causes errors, but we try to keep it the same)
•    The enumeration options
•    The order of enumeration options
•    Avalibility for classifications

author: eldelion
content:
What kind of commands do we need to assist this workflow?
The official JSON interface separates the options op properties to two categories:
•    the property name / description / value definition part {propertyDefinition}
•    the avalibilty for classifications part {PropertyDefinitionAvailability}
That leaves:
•    the display order of enumeration options (I think it is separate from the enum value?)
•    the order of the list of properties Maybe call it PropertyDefinitionTree? 

And for all of those we need a Get, Set, and a create and delete for property definitions and groups.
Implemented Official:
•    GetPropertyIds/GetAllPropertyIds/GetAllPropertyNames
•    GetPropertyGroups
•    GetDetailsOfProperties
•    GetPropertyDefinitionAvailability
Implemented Tapir:
•    CreatePropertyGroups
Needed:
•    CreateProperties(parameter: propertyDefinition) – the new property is avalible for no calssifications
•    SetDetailsOfProperties(parameter: propertyID, propertyDefinition) 
•    SetDefinitionAvailability
•    DeleteProperty
•    DeletePropertyGroup
•    GetDisplayOrderOfEnumOptions (is this really a thing? Or how does it look like under the hood?)
•    SetDisplayOrderOfEnumOptions
•    GetPropertyDefinitionTree
•    SetPropertyDefinitionTree (can rearrange, but not delete/create)

author: tlorantfy
content:
Tapir sends JSON commands to Archicad and Archicad respond with JSON.
So currently Archicad is not able to tell anything to Tapir, unless Tapir asks Archicad.
This means Archicad is not able to notify Tapir that an element was changed. So Tapir is not able to react to element changes.
Tapir client would have to implement polling to be able to do that... I don't recommend you to try that, that will be "non-functioning terrible" as you said.

I had an idea. Tapir could have a RegisterCommandOnElementChange command. The client could be able to register a script to be executed when an element was changed.
For example:
```RegisterCommandOnElementChange('python on_element_changed.py $elementId')```
So Archicad will execute that, replacing $elementId placeholder with the id of the changed element.
That's feasible, but I don't know how useful is that. Anyway, surely not on the top of the list.

author: eldelion
content:
Yes, I think we need a way to search properties. I would prefer the name search method, for the following reasons:
•    Easier to implement
•    Safer. If you create a definition, save it and then reuse it later the 3-12 element can easily be a totally different property. The same name is usually used for the same property. If it is not yet created in the document, we get an error, and the script stopps. It doesn't write something accidentally to the property that happens to be at the 3-12 position.
•    The name search based approach works better with a list / tree of input names. We should consider the use-case, where property names come from a script, not a human selects it manually

author: tlorantfy
content:
Guys, I've been thinking about the GetPropertyValues node.
It should have 2 inputs, a propertyId and the elements. There should be only one output, the values of elements which is a list if strings.
The size of the output list must match the size of the input list of elements.

But what happens in case one of the input elements does not have the given property? The node must return something for that element also. It's bad to return empty string or "error", because those can be valid property values.
I will try to return null, but I doubt Grasshopper will be able to handle that (probably the next node which gets that as input will fail).
I have an ugly solution idea: return empty string, but make a 2nd output which tells us which elements had issues. It would be hard to use that 2nd output... But maybe in most of the workflows nobody cares there were issues 😁
Do you have any idea how to handle this? What would be Grasshopper-like?

author: eldelion

Advantages:
•    Pyinstaller can build an executeable from a NiceGUI app
•    But it is actually a backed + frontend combo, so after figuring out a way to send reqests from the web, your apps can run on a server
•    While Custom Tkinter looks good, it always looks like CustomTkinter. You can Customize NiceGUI much more.
•    It has a lot of ready-to-use widgets from a big frontend library (Quasar by default, but you van use Vue components as well). 
•    It uses python for frontend + backend – you don’t need to learn JavaScript
Disadvantages:
•    While much simpler than let’s say Django + React, more complicated than Tkinter
•    Even a simple app has a full server running in the back, probably not the best for performance

author: dkovacs9689
content:
<@996687564226445353>,
I posted this a while back about a much more simplistic little app (compared to what you can do 😄 ).

You can see at the beginning I had a dialog where you can pick a running Archicad (I made my own solution instead of the MultiConnAC, because I was using the “ac-lib” library). 

You can see that the dialog just cycles through the ports, and doesn’t list all the open Archicads. That was my original plan, but the only way I knew how was to try and connect to Archicad on each port, and see if there was a response or if it timed out. But that meant that for every port I iterated through with an open Archicad I got a response in a fraction of a second, and for every timed out port I needed to wait 3 seconds, so overall, checking all available ports took me a minute (3 sec x nrOfPorts).

In your solution, do you just wait that time when you refresh, or do you have some kind of solution for quickly checking all the possible ports?

author: eldelion
content:
I found 2 ways to decrese the time it takes to refresh:
- concurrency. There are 20 ports to check. Send out 20 reqests simultaniously, and wait for the responses. Python has the built-in  asyncio module to handle it.
-the time you wait until you consider a request failed can be configured. As AC instances are local, it can probably be decresed significantly. 
I haven't played with the timeout numbers yet as I don't know what is a safe number, but even without it scanning all ports take less than a secound

author: dkovacs9689
content:
Very interesting.
What is the advantage of using your own automation over the built-in backups?

author: 1yur
content:
There're around 60 teamwork files on our server, and there are almost 40 average active projects while the workday.
During the years of experience, we've noticed, that native backup process is pretty overwhelming for the system. Especially for such great numbers. And an average size of project is about 2-3 Gb. Some exceedes even 5-7 Gb. So, while BIMcloud is trying to make a backup of these projects, it heavily overloads disc queue on the server side and this could lead to freezes or crashes. I guess it caused by strange (ineffective?) queue of the backuping process.

There are two solutions for this: to set asynchronous backup schedules for each of the projects, or to do it's another way. The first option seems fine, when the numbers aren't so great, but it's pretty hard to manage manually (taking into account that we're using BIMcloud basic). So we've taken a 2nd option and made a python script to grab a backups of modified projects and transfer them to Google Drive.

content:
Hello Community!

First off, big thanks to everyone for the amazing work here! I’m a big fan of Tapir and use it as an extension to the Archicad Python API. I can really see the potential in the plugins you’re developing.

Currently, I’m working on an architectural project where we need to place 3D objects that reference detail drawings. Our team heavily relies on Archicad’s regular detail objects, which link to a drawing and include a 2D polygon. I’d like to be able to query these detail objects via Python and extract their GDL parameters to see if I can enrich the Archicad model (e.g., by adding URLs to the drawings or placing 3D objects), or even enhance the exported IFC model.

Tapir exposes the "GetGDLParametersOfElements" command, but unfortunately, it seems to exclude objects with the "Marker" subtype. Are there any plans to extend this command to support GDL parameters for these objects? I’m proficient in Python and C#, though not in C++, but I’d be happy to help in any way I can!

Thanks in advance! 😊
Small example how I get the detail object:
```python
import archicad
import aclib

try:
    conn = archicad.ACConnection.connect()
    assert conn

    acc = conn.commands
    act = conn.types
    acu = conn.utilities

except:
    raise RuntimeError("No ArchiCAD running!")

elementsResponse = aclib.RunTapirCommand(
    'GetAllElements', {})
elements = elementsResponse['elements']
detailsOfElements = aclib.RunTapirCommand(
```

author: kovacsv
content: The new library API is written in a more modern way. Instead of returning error codes, every new function returns an `ACAPI::Result` object. In this case, the return value type of the `GetName` function is `ACAPI::Result<GS::UniString>`. The `ACAPI::Result` object is a wrapper that contains the value (in this case, the name) or an error code if the operation was not successful.

author: kovacsv
content: You can check if an `ACAPI::Result` object has no error by calling the `result.IsOk ()` function. If it contains an error, but you are trying to access the value, it will cause a crash. This is helpful during development, since you are able to immediately detect if you've missed an error checking.

author: tlorantfy
content:
Tapir is based on Archicad API, so Tapir can do what is available via Archicad API.
I checked your requests.
(1) The display names of the parameters are available, so it's easy, see uDescname in API_AddParType
(2) The locked information is available too. These are the available flags:
- fixed (fixed param, could not delete, but can modify its value)
- disabled (I think this is the locked information)
- hidden
- hiddenFromScript
(3) I think this is **not** available via API 😦 But for example if the type of the parameter is "BuildingMaterial", then it's an index of an existing building material, so you can get the number of building materials and that way you will know the minimum and maximum value (attributes are indexed 1-based, so minimum is 1, maximum is the count of building materials).

```python
from archicad import ACConnection

conn = ACConnection.connect()
acc = conn.commands
act = conn.types

propertyGroup = 'COMMON (Materials)'
propertyName = 'Porosity'
propertyUserId = act.PropertyUserId("UserDefined", [propertyGroup, propertyName] )

print(acc.GetDetailsOfProperties(propertyIds))
```

```
import aclib

```

author: fbumaye
content:
a very simple example to create automatically building materials:

```python
# server.py
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
import aclib

# Create an MCP server
mcp = FastMCP("Demo")


@mcp.resource("greeting://{name}")
def get_greeting(name: str) -> str:
    """Get a personalized greeting"""
    return f"Hello, {name}!"


@mcp.tool()
def create_building_materials(building_material_name: str) -> str:
    buildMats = {
        'name': building_material_name,
        'id': str(1),
        'manufacturer': 'Tapir',
        'description': 'This is an example Building Material',
        'connPriority': 1,
        'cutFillIndex': 1,
        'cutFillPen': 2,
        'cutFillBackgroundPen': 3,
        'cutSurfaceIndex': 4,
        'thermalConductivity': 1.0,
        'density': 2.0,
        'heatCapacity': 3.0,
        'embodiedEnergy': 4.0,
        'embodiedCarbon': 5.0
    }

    result = aclib.RunTapirCommand('CreateBuildingMaterials', {
        'buildingMaterialDataArray': [buildMats],
        'overwriteExisting': True
    })

    # result = aclib.RunCommand('API.GetBuildingMaterialAttributes', {
    #     'attributeIds': result['attributeIds']
    # })

    print('New building materials:\n' + aclib.JsonDumpDictionary(result))
    return aclib.JsonDumpDictionary(result)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp.run()
````

author: eldelion
content:
Hello Fbumaye!

Just to add to what Tibor said.
You can define depenedencies 2 ways with  uv:
1. - inline script dependencies. These are at the top of the script, witch is good for standalone scripts as they don1t get misplaced. You don't need to manually edit these, uv can do that for you: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/scripts/#declaring-script-dependencies
2. - uv looks for a pyproject.toml file in the same folder as the script. This is actually the standard way to manage dependencies in python. With Tapir palettes current structure (many scripts in a folder) it should only contain common dependencies. (managing projects: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/projects/)

Setting this up, I ran into a few things that can be improved to make things smoother:
• reloading should first empty temp/Tapir. Currently, after a rename, the old files remain
• __init__.py should be added to the future list of ignored files
• something is broken with the error messages – there is no dialog for errors; they just appear in the report. Sorry
• the GitHub token (PAT) is now only used for downloading the scripts. But when using a private repo, it is needed to:
 o see the source code with the source button
 o but more importantly, to access private package dependencies. If I understand correctly, it is possible to add the token from the config file to the ENV variables of the process that ExecuteScript creates: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/environment/#uv_github_token. That way, uv should be able to install company packages.
• I previously confused two things since I always had a virtual environment. uv has two distinct “modes”:
 o using it to manage a virtual environment. This is when the pyproject.toml is used, and this way you can link to files up to the source folder of the project.
 o using it to run scripts. This way only the inline script metadata is used, and you can only import from subdirectories. – Tibor was 100% right.

The "setter" nodes now have "Execute" button, the "getter" nodes still have "Refresh" button.
ConnectArchicad GH node has both "AutoRefresh" and "AutoExecute" **optional** inputs, by default "AutoRefresh" is true,  "AutoExecute" is false.

The node will show "Waiting for manual execution" information message untill the user clicks "Execute".

author: eldelion
content:
I’m not 100% sure about what you want to do exactly, but it is probably possible. There are 2 challenges:
1.    Archicad communicates on localhost. So you need to have something running where you want to strart up  projects that can recive communication from outside, and than open up the archicads/send requests to it.
2.    A lot of different dialogs can appear during startup, that will stop the process. You need to handle those. Multiconn archicad has a dialog handler, but it only works on windows, and on the international version. 
Opening up a teamwork project with a location/user/pass is handled in multiconn archicad, but if you don’t want to use it, the trick is this line – the project location passed as command line  argument needs to be this: f"teamwork://{single_quote(teamwork_credentials.username)}:{single_quote(teamwork_credentials.password{double_quote(self.serverAddress)}/{double_quote(self.projectPath)}"

author: bschwb
content:
Hi <@720568379823620106>! There's also the alternative of `ACAPI_Element_GetRelations` (https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/group___element.html#ga24c922dec98f8f6412b0db35620b0df3). I've used that for my room coverings add-on. The Zone Boundary Query is available since AC27. I haven't used it yet, but looked into it recently. I think it additionally gives you the actual planar surface where e.g. wall and zone touch.
On the other hand the Room relations don't give you the actual surface, but they give you which part of the wall makes the border for the zone.

For what you described, I think both should give you the relevant information of which walls are bordering the zone. But to be safe maybe it's worth testing both and see which info you can handle better.

author: eldelion
content:
Welcome Timon!

Automatically creating a simulation model from an architectural model is quite the challenge! Good luck with that 🙂
I'm not  sure what is the exact problem where you are stuck, so I'll just list a few can/can't dos that seam relevant.

What is possible with Tapir/python api:
- get polygon outline of rooms with holes. I think Honybee needs touching room faces, a grometry based on polylines is probably easier to offset than a triangulated one
- get property values of pretty much everithing
- get the details of attributes, so you can calculate thermal resistance from materials / composites. (probably not practical to do so except for projects with like hundreds or thousands of composites)
- get elements related to zones (if their related zone property is correct)

what you cant do (but the C++ API can, so might be implemented in the future)
- get actual zone geometry (but the official connection covers you for that)
- get the surfaces of each element touching a zone, matched to the element

content:
Official Python API : Release notes
29.3000

Here's an overview of the changes included in this release:

    PropertyTypes
        A new property called NormalPropertyValue has been added.
    Types
        A new enum value called All has been added to ElementTypes enum.
    GetElementsRelatedToZones
        The elementTypes command parameter is now required.
            In cases where elementTypes was not used previously, use it with the newly added All value.
    GetPropertyValuesOfElements
        A new parameter called onlySupportedTypes has been added.
            Optional parameter. When it is set to true, only elements with types that are supported by any other JSON API command will be returned.

author: tlorantfy
content:
So basically there are 2 types of commands:
The "official" Graphisoft implemented JSON commands.
And the Tapir JSON commands 💪 

Unfortunately Graphisoft has already announced that they won't create new commands. That's the main reason why Tapir community started to create our own commands.

author: tlorantfy
content:
SendArchicadCommand("<CommandName>", CommandJSONParameters)
This executes the given "official" command (documentation at https://archicadapi.graphisoft.com/JSONInterfaceDocumentation )

SendArchicadAddOnCommand("TapirCommand", "<CommandName>", CommandJSONParameters)
This executes the Tapir command (documentation at https://enzyme-apd.github.io/tapir-archicad-automation/archicad-addon/ )

author: ferencz_tamas
content: hi guys, I have a few questions regarding ElemsByType grasshopper component. 1. Should "Group" type select the groups in Archicad? 2. Does "CutPlane stand for section marks? 3. Then what "SectElem" is for?

author: tlorantfy
content:
<@689040789866807369> , I checked it in the documentation of Archicad API, see API_ElemTypeID enumeration here: https://graphisoft.github.io/archicad-api-devkit/group___element.html#ga2502601bf26ffc7abc608f6988da4d91
1. API_GroupID means the group of elements. So basically a Group is kinda special element in Archicad API. But I think it's OK that ElemsByType GH node does not return groups now. Maybe we should implement GetGroupOfElement and GetElementsInGroup commands/nodes.
2. API_CutPlaneID means section element. So your guess was correct, CutPlane is for the section marks. I checked it and ElemsByType GH node works OK for this, it returns the guids of section marks.
3. API_SectElemID means an element in a section view. So in Archicad in section view (and probably in elevation too) there are not walls/doors/etc. elements, but everything is a SectElem (like "vetület" in hungarian) and each SectElem has link to a parent element which is the wall/door/etc.
So basically ElemsByType GH node with SectElem input will return you guids only if you set a Section/Elevation for the Databases input.

author: tlorantfy
content:
Action items:
- Remove the "Group" from that popup.
- Rename "CutPlane" to "Section".
- Remove "SectElem", and access the parent elements in Tapir AddOn (hide that Archicad section element magic from Tapir users).
So currently if the input database is a Section and Wall type is given, then it won't return you any wall, even if there are walls visible on the given Section. It's because you should use SectElem type and get the parent elements of the returned SectElems to get the walls (it's not possible to get the parent element yet).
But I'm planning to hide that magic from the user, so Tapir will be intelligent and if the input type is Wall and the input database is a Section, then it will automatically return the guids of the parent walls of the SectElems.

author: tlorantfy
content:
Unfortunately it's an Archicad API restriction:
There is ACAPI_Attribute_Create function, that can create 1 attribute and after that the Archicad user interface updates itself.
So if you create 100 attributes using CreateLayers command, then the Archicad user interface will update itself 100 times, that takes long 🙁
And there is ACAPI_Attribute_DeleteMore, that can create multiple attributes and after that the Archicad user interface updates itself only once.
The only thing we can do is to ask Graphisoft to improve the API, maybe <@844197976430608424> can help with the lobbying activity 🙂

author: tlorantfy
content:
Reindexing is not available via Archicad API.
Somebody has already got this request, see https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/319
I've investigated it and that functionality is not in Archicad API 🙁
We can delete, create and modify layers and change the layers of elements one-by-one.
So you can do the following:
Let's say there is a layer with index 5 and you would like to have it index 2.
At first you have to check whether there is already a layer on index 2.
If there is no layer on index 2, then you have to make sure that index 2 is the lowest free index and then create a new layer with the same details. Finally delete the original layer AND modify all elements which referenced to layer 5 to use layer 2 instead.
If there was already a layer on index 2, then you have to move that first.
It's too complicated 😄

author: tlorantfy
content:
GDL is a misterious animal 😅
Let me give you some background:
Every GDL based element has a so called "parameter script" and that runs every time when any of the parameters is changed.
Let's assume there is parameter X and parameter Y. The parameter script can define that X always must be the double of Y. "X=2*Y"
So it's totally expected that you successfully changed the value X, but in the end the value of X is unchanged (because the parameter script modified it).

author: eldelion
content:
By the way, how concurrency works in addons/archicad? After an event triggers, you probably want to send a buch of requests as a response. 
Get reqests should be relatively threadsafe, so they might be a good candidate to put to a background thread, so they do not block archicad while they execute.

author: eldelion
content: I suspect the server that intercepts json requests is on the main thread and syncronous. But maybe there is a way 😀

author: eldelion
content:
Thinking about it the Json server being synchronous might not be a problem. A possible solution popped to my mind:
1.    We add a flag to a request (computeInBackground), or create a command that alters the state of the Tapir addon (ComputeNextCommandInBackground)
2.    The server immediately sends a response yielding the main thread that only contains a randomly generated token 
3.    The background thread starts to work, and then eventually, when it has the solution send it with the token attached
It is still a question if a background thread can even access the main archicad database, or if a complicated solution like that is even worth it ofc…

author: eldelion
content:
I haven't done any decisive testing, but I have a hunch that the number of elements in the archicad database significantly effects how long a get request takes (the problem is with expression based properties?). 
In a project I'm working on I regularly read around 20-25 properties of 40-60 000 elements per file.  I was thinking about doing the syncronization on the new element change trigger, but we sometimes change the properties of a few thousand elements together. But on my project the reading speed is only around 300-400 properties per secound. That would mean up to 5-20 minutes syncronization when ~5 000- 15 000 elements are changed. That is  too slow even for a background thread.
But on smaller scale projects real time syncronization seams like an interesting possibility.

content: Well... I think for usecases where long syncronization is a regular thing (like mine) the answer is not doing the live syncronization 🙁 . But I like your idea for usecases where it can occasionally happen. Right now on the python side, based on Tibor's code if we modify 100 elements at once we are reciveing a 100 events one-by-one. Gathering up those, and sending in an array would give the python code the nececary information based on a simple len() function to display a notification.

author: tlorantfy
content:
Now I see that Archicad does the following when the user modifies multiple elements (lets say 100 elements):
It sends a Begin event to Tapir AddOn then it sends the 100 event for the elements one by one, and finally it sends an End event to Tapir AddOn.
I will modify the Tapir AddOn to not forward the events one by one to the script, but save them and send them only when it got the End event.
<@558945647085223946> , do you think it can help?

author: eldelion
content:
Yeah, that behaviour is more in line with how I would expect it to behave personally. 
While sending the events one-by-one theoretically allows your code to do something as soon as the first arrives, in most cases that something would involve Archicad – which is unresponsive until the whole operation has finished. Sending the events from a single command in batches is more performant, and has extra information, so I would go with that.

author: daviiiiidave
content:
New Tapir commands for renovation workflows

I've been looking for a solution to this for a long time and finally just vibed it out with Claude — I'm not a coder, so this is very much a proof of concept, but it works!

I built three new add-on commands for automating composite/renovation workflows in Archicad. Everything was done locally — the commands are on a feature branch and not yet merged into the main repo.

GetCompositeOfElement — reads the composite structure (name, GUID, skins with type, thickness, building material) from a Wall, Slab, Roof or Shell element.

SetElementComposite — assigns a composite attribute to an element by GUID.

CreateCompositeVariant — clones an existing composite and overrides individual skins:

sets the skin's frame pen
optionally clones the building material with a suffix (e.g. "Glaswolle → Glaswolle Abbruch") and overrides the cut fill background pen — idempotent, so running it twice reuses the existing material
On top of that I wrote a small Tkinter UI script (RenovationSkinMarker.py) that ties everything together: select a wall, run the script, pick per-skin status (Abbruch / Neubau / unchanged) from a table with live color feedback, enter a variant name, and hit "Create Variant" — the script calls all three commands in sequence and optionally assigns the new composite to the wall immediately.

Not perfect yet, but the proof of concept is there. Would love feedback from people who know the API better!

Requires Tapir Add-On ≥ 1.3.3.

author: daviiiiidave
content:
Renovation Skin Marker — Update

Been busy improving the script since the last post! Here's what's new:

Multi-wall support — select multiple walls at once, they all get the same composite variant assigned in one go. If they have different composites, you get a warning first.

Smarter error handling — if a variant with that name already exists, the script asks if you want to assign it anyway instead of just throwing an error.

Automatic folder placement — the new composite variant is automatically placed in the same folder as the original in the Composites dialog. No manual sorting needed.

New UI — switched from plain tkinter to CustomTkinter for a cleaner look that matches the Archicad style. Added a disclaimer dialog on startup.

Correct skin types — Kern / Bekleidung / Andere are now read directly from the API flags instead of guessing by position.

Still all local, still vibing with Claude. 🙂

A difference, though, is that after 2001 the web was essentially free to use. AI, by contrast, remains inherently computationally expensive, so the analogy only holds if inference costs continue to fall dramatically. If they do, both a bubble and the long-term relevance of the technology could be true at the same time.

author: __iota__
content:
I didn't manage to modifiy the json file but Claude found a solution. I'll copy paste what it "told" me: I used Claude to help me diagnose and work around this issue, so I'll do my best to explain what was found, but some of the technical details are beyond my full understanding.

The problem/recap
On my machine (macOS 15.7.7, ArchiCAD 27), Tapir's automatic uv update downloads a version of uv that crashes when launched from within ArchiCAD's process environment. The crash appears to be related to a macOS version check inside uv that fails in this context.
Additionally, even when uv manages to run, the Python it uses (system Python 3.9) has a Tcl/Tk 8.5 library that crashes on tkinter initialization when the process is launched as a subprocess of a Cocoa app like ArchiCAD. The crash happens at TkpInit and terminates the process with SIGABRT.

The workaround Claude created
Since the uvLocation field in config.json accepts a path to any executable, Claude created a small shell script (a "wrapper") at that path. This wrapper pretends to be uv — it responds correctly to --version so Tapir's version check passes — but instead of running the real uv, it calls /usr/local/bin/python3 (Python 3.13, which has Tk 8.6 and works correctly from ArchiCAD):

#!/bin/bash
if [[ "$1" == "--version" ]]; then
    echo "uv 0.8.4 (e176e1714 2025-07-30)"
    exit 0
fi
if [[ "$1" == "run" && "$2" == "--script" ]]; then
    shift 2
    exec /usr/local/bin/python3 "$@"
fi
To prevent Tapir from overwriting this wrapper when it auto-updates uv, Claude also set a macOS immutable flag on the file (chflags uchg), which blocks any write to that file until the flag is explicitly removed.

author: __iota__
content:
Why modifying config.json alone wasn't enough
* uvLocation can redirect to a different uv binary, but there is no option to disable the auto-update — so Tapir would eventually overwrite any uv we point it to.
* uvLocation expects a uv-compatible interface (uv run --script ...), so we can't point it directly to Python — that's why a wrapper was needed to translate the call.
* There is no pythonLocation or disableUvAutoUpdate option in the current config schema.

Feature requests
1. A disableUvAutoUpdate option in config.json — so users with compatibility issues can pin their uv version without needing workarounds.
2. A pythonLocation option — to let users specify which Python interpreter to use, bypassing uv entirely for environments where uv is problematic.

author: __iota__
content:
So I want to implement sublines deletion in ModifyMeshes via ACAPI_Element_Change and I'm stuck. When passing sublines: [], I want the mesh to have zero level lines. Creating a mesh with no sublines works fine (null handles in ACAPI_Element_Create). But modifying an existing mesh to remove all its sublines — can't figure it out.

Everything I've tried still returns got: 2 instead of got: 0:

null handles + APIMemoMask_MeshLevel → ignored by ArchiCAD
1-byte handle + APIMemoMask_MeshLevel → GS minimum physical allocation = 8 bytes → 8/4 = 2 sublines
BMhSetSize(h, 0) → same 8-byte minimum
element mask only (nSubLines=0 without APIMemoMask_MeshLevel) → nSubLines not updated
ACAPI_Element_ChangeMemo with empty memo → ignored
handle with sentinel value -1 → ArchiCAD counts by handle size, not by value
Is removing all level lines from an existing mesh even possible through the API? If yes, how?

I shared a modification of the set details command in order to be able to modify display order. This part of Archicad is not consistent at all 😭 . ArchiCAD enforces a hard minimum of level 7 for openings embedded in a

reached by stepping the host element up (the opening follows), then
stepping it back down (the opening stays elevated). Reset 
on an elevated opening must also go through the host.

content:
Claude is more than capable to do that with the MCP, it just needs some convincing. It needs to find the SetPropertiesOfElements command, and use that.
The full schema of all commands takes around 137 000 tokens, whitch would will up Claude's context window, so the MCP uses a discover/call pattern, where it searches for the right tool until it finds it, or fails to find it. I don't know if I can make it smarter, but I definitely can achive this lvl of dumb with a much simpler approach. author: tlorantfy
content:
Operating on Elevation/Section is a little bit complicated.
In Archicad, under the hood, when you see for example a Wall on a Section/Elevation view, then that's not a Wall but a SectionElement which was generated for the wall.
So when you create a Label/Text for the Wall in Archicad on Section/Elevation, then you create the Label/Text for the SectionElement instead and not for the Wall itself.
The same should happen via API/Tapir...
I believe that's why you got error, because you input the Wall's guid and not the related SectionElement's guid.
I will try to fix this inside Tapir. So Tapir should be able to detect that you are on a Section/Elevation view and your input is a Wall, then it should automatically replace the given Wall's guid with the curresponding SectionElement's guid.

author: turit_
content:
The first test was successful. I found this to be the most suitable method for the time being.

1. export xml and re-indexing (starting from 1000).
2. importing re-indexed layers based on index; the suffix "(1)" is added to the names.
3. Running the tapir program.
 3a. Checking if every layer has a corresponding pair.
 3b. Moving elements.
 3c. Deleting old layers.
 3d. Removing "(1)" from the names.
4. Importing template layers into the plan (indexes 2–100).
5. Running the tapir program.
 5a. Migration tab: select the new layer range and the current range (2–100 and 1000+).
 5b. Mapping table: if a layer is not found, a suitable choice can be made manually; the mapping can also be exported to Excel and re-imported.
 5c. Execution.
 5d. Deleting layers with indexes 1000+.

author: ooki_85834_38875
content:
Hi everyone, this is my first post here!
Using Claude Code, I built a set of scripts that automatically generate MEP piping in Archicad. The MEP route generation commands in Tapir were written by Claude Code as well (I'm running my own build of the add-on).

Each of these runs with a single click:
1. Select the sanitary fixtures and the morph at the downstream end of the drain line → drainage piping is generated
2. Select the AC indoor units and the outdoor unit morphs → refrigerant piping is generated
3. Select the ventilation equipment → exhaust ducts and hoods are generated

For 1 and 2, any route that goes to another floor is forced to run through the pipe shaft (PS).
The approach: I keep the relevant building codes and piping design standards in Obsidian as a knowledge base, then have Claude Code generate a dedicated Python script from that knowledge and register it in the Tapir palette.
Hope this is useful to someone!
https://youtu.be/P1uSpDI6rbU

author: ooki_85834_38875
content:
Hi Abraham,

Thanks for the encouragement — I just submitted the pull request to the official Tapir GitHub!

One thing worth mentioning: 3 days ago (2026-07-25) the maintainer himself merged a full official MEP command suite (PR #473), covering creation, querying and connecting of MEP elements. It's a great addition, but the description explicitly called out "preference-table management" as out of scope for now.

That's exactly the gap my PR fills: GetMEPPreferenceTables lists the circular cross-section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, description) for the Piping or Ventilation domain. In practice, when you place or modify a pipe/duct route with CreateMEPRoutingElements / ModifyMEPRoutingElements, you have to specify the cross section via a referenceId — but there was no way to look up which referenceId corresponds to which diameter. This command closes that gap, so you can resolve "I want a 100mm pipe" to the right referenceId before creating the route.

Regarding compiling on all 25+ Archicad versions — like the rest of the official MEP group, this command requires Archicad 28+ to actually function, but it still registers and compiles cleanly on older versions (25–27); it just returns APIERR_NOTSUPPORTED there, following the same pattern the maintainer already uses elsewhere in the add-on.

Let's see how the review goes — I'll keep you posted!

Best regards,
Ooki

author: daviiiiidave
content:
What I found digging through the AC29 DevKit: the API has had exactly this relation since
AC26 — ACAPI_Element_GetRelations. For a door/window it returns API_DoorRelation /
API_WindowRelation with fromRoom/toRoom zone GUIDs (pass-through doors have both, exterior
openings one). Queried from the zone side, API_RoomRelation.elementsGroupedByType returns
all elements in the zone grouped by type. Curtain wall panels have the same from/to-room
relation. So the data model is all there — it's just not surfaced in schedules, and (as far
as I can see) not in Tapir either: 1.5.6 has GetZoneBoundaries (geometric boundaries via
ZoneBoundaryQuery) and GetConnectedElements (ownership only: wall→door/window etc.), but
no wrapper for ACAPI_Element_GetRelations.

author: gr_cad_85891
content:
here is explanation from our friend Claude 😉  

A place to find and share Tapir scripts and Archicad add-ons, built for the
community and free to use.

**Browsing needs no account.** Search, filter by category or Archicad version,
and download. Nothing to sign up for.

**Publishing needs a free GitHub account.** Fill in one form: name, description,
category, which Archicad versions it works with, and a download link. Add
screenshots and a video if you have them. Automated checks run and your listing
goes live, usually within a couple of minutes. No waiting for approval.

**Your listing stays yours.** It is filed under your own GitHub name, so you can
edit or remove it whenever you like, and nobody else can change it. Your contact
details carry over, so the second script you publish is quicker than the first.

**Questions live with the script.** Every listing has a comment section, and
those comments also appear in the forum, so all discussion is searchable in one
place. You can start a topic there too.

**Vote for what you find useful.** One vote per account, and you can take it
back. It helps good scripts surface.

**Downloads are checked.** You can host your file anywhere. Every download is
fingerprinted when first seen and re-checked every hour. If the file behind a
published version changes, the listing is flagged and the download is pulled
until a proper new version is released. Still, these are scripts that run inside
your Archicad, so read what you download and try it on a copy first.

**Money goes to the author.** Scripts can be free, free with a contribution
link, or paid. In every case you pay the author directly through their own link.
The site never handles a payment or takes a cut.

Not affiliated with Graphisoft. Archicad is a trademark of Graphisoft SE.

author: heartbreaker2323
content:
"Direct answer : it's not simulating keystrokes or clicking into the text box — it uses Archicad's own official developer API (ACAPI, the same interface Graphisoft provides to every add-on) to edit the element's data directly. The mechanism, step by step:

Identify the element — every object in an Archicad file has a unique internal ID (a GUID). Zendsign already knows which element it's correcting from the audit it just ran.
Read the current data — ACAPI_Element_Get/ACAPI_Element_GetMemo pulls the element's full record into memory, including its text content and formatting (font, size, pen color, spacing).
Modify only the text field — the new text replaces the old one in that in-memory copy. Formatting fields are explicitly re-asserted unchanged, so a correction can't accidentally alter font/size/color.
Commit the change — ACAPI_Element_Change, wrapped in ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand. This is the important part: it's a real, undoable Archicad transaction, exactly like an edit you'd make by hand — it shows up in Archicad's own Undo history, participates in Teamwork reservation rules, etc. It's not a side-channel hack.
Read it back and verify — after writing, Zendsign re-reads the element and confirms the new value actually matches what was requested, rather than just trusting that the API call returned "no error."
And before any of this runs, the user sees a confirm dialog showing the current value → proposed value and has to explicitly approve it — nothing gets written silently.

So the short version: it's the same official mechanism any Archicad add-on (including Graphisoft's own tools) uses to edit the model — read the element, change the field in memory, commit it as a normal undoable operation, verify it stuck.

author: heartbreaker2323
content:
This is the exact bug class we spent nine debugging attempts on for its own Correct Text feature — I can give your colleague the actual working fix, not a guess.

Text content on an existing element (the "NoError but doesn't persist" case):

The fix that actually worked had two parts, and both were required together — neither alone was enough:

Build the memo from scratch, don't fetch-then-modify. Don't reuse the memo you read via ACAPI_Element_GetMemo — construct a brand-new blank API_ElementMemo and only set memo.textContent. Fetching the existing memo and modifying it in place was one of the failed attempts.
Explicitly mask and reassert the sibling formatting fields, even though you're not changing them. Masking only textContent/APIMemoMask_TextContent silently failed. The working call also sets ACAPI_ELEMENT_MASK_SET for pen, faceBits, font, size, spacing, widthFactor, charSpaceFactor — and populates them in the element struct with their current values (read via ACAPI_Element_Get beforehand), not left default/zeroed. It's as if Archicad's internal validation for a text-content write wants the whole style block asserted as a unit, not a single isolated field.

author: heartbreaker2323
content:
One more thing that mattered for us: whether the element is monostyle vs multistyle (i.e. has real memo.paragraphs/runs) matters a lot. For multistyle text, swapping textContent while leaving the old paragraphs[i].from/range describing the old string's length causes a real rejection — APIERR_PAROVERFLOW (-2130312713, "paragraph end offset runs over the content length") — if the new text is a different length. So if your colleague's text is multistyle, they need to also update the paragraph/run from/range to the new content's actual length before writing.

arrowData.arrowVisibility not persisting while framed does:

I haven't hit this exact field myself, but it smells like the same class of bug as the text case above: masking only the one nested field you want to change isn't enough — some nested structs seem to require every field within that same nested struct to be masked and reasserted together, not just the one that's actually changing. Worth trying: mask every field in arrowData (not just arrowVisibility), populated with its current values except the one actually changing — same "reassert the whole unit" pattern that fixed the text case.

And in both cases: confirm the write is wrapped in ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand. Zendsign's own working code always wraps the ACAPI_Element_Change call in one — if theirs isn't, that alone could explain "returns NoError but doesn't stick," since changes made outside an explicit undoable transaction can behave inconsistently.

author: weltmaister.
content:
Just published two open-source Claude Agent Skills for driving Archicad through Tapir - MIT, free to use:

https://github.com/weltmaister/archicad-agent-skills

**abstracting-building-models** - turns drawings/scans/PDFs into a structured parametric building model: raster calibration, dimension-chain extraction, evidence + uncertainty tracking.

**archicad-automation** - drives Archicad over Tapir's JSON API: hand-verified payload shapes for the most-used commands, known crash traps, per-release version gates (what exists since 1.5.4 / 1.5.6 / 1.5.8 and how to probe the connected instance), and a strict "never trust the return value - verify by read-back" discipline.

They're field guides distilled from a summer of live testing on AC26/AC28 - and a handful of upstream PRs that came out of it.

A note on why the examples talk HTTP directly to the Tapir port rather than through the (excellent) MCP server: these skills grew alongside upstream development, during weeks when new commands were merging almost daily - the raw port was simply the shortest path to test a command the day it landed and to probe exactly what the connected build supports. That's a snapshot of a fast-moving phase, not an architecture statement: the knowledge in these skills is transport-agnostic and applies 1:1 when you drive Tapir through the MCP server - which is the more comfortable setup for typed tools and multi-instance discovery, and where a lot of this knowledge could eventually live built-in.

Feedback and PRs welcome!

author: ooki_85834_38875
content:
I've built a tool with Claude Code that automatically models construction sequences from a design BIM model!

1. One click on the "Auto Construction Steps" script registered in the Tapir palette generates everything.
2. Construction elements that don't exist in the original model — blinding concrete + crushed stone base, the excavation volume, and the site terrain for the construction phase — are generated automatically by reading the building model.
3. The objects needed for those models — temporary site hoarding, simplified exterior scaffolding, and earth retaining walls — were built by Claude Code as custom GDL objects. These custom objects are placed automatically too.
4. Dedicated layers and layer combinations are all created automatically, including intersection group numbers so that unwanted intersections are avoided.
5. Both reinforced concrete and steel structures are supported.
6. Besides native Archicad files, it also works with IFC data from GLOOBE (another BIM authoring tool) and from Helios (a cost estimation tool).
The middle part of the video is sped up 4x, but a model of this size takes about 3 minutes to generate!
https://youtu.be/OtSKvGp2_EU

author: ooki_85834_38875
content:
I also had Claude Code automate the creation of a construction assembly video from the construction step model I posted earlier!

1. Claude Code reads the construction steps out of Archicad through Tapir, links the model into Unreal Engine with the Datasmith Exporter, and generates the video automatically.
2. I describe what I want in the video to Claude Code entirely in plain language. I watch the draft it renders and simply tell it what to change — things like "change the camera angle" or "make the scaffolding rise from the bottom."
